speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, I'm Susan Kerr, and now for something completely different.
zh: 你好，我是 Susan Kerr，现在来点完全不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been an iconographer and designer.
zh: 我一直是个图标制作人和设计师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've worked on a lot of tech projects, and I want to talk about
zh: 我参与过很多科技项目，我想谈谈

speaker: Unknown
en: A tech startup I worked for when even though the Macintosh group was part of Apple, but I think a lot of the experiences resonate with some of the topics that I've heard here today.
zh: 我为之工作过的一家科技初创公司，尽管 Macintosh 团队是 Apple 的一部分，但我认为很多经历与我今天在这里听到的一些话题产生共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been doing this for a while and love it.
zh: 所以我做这行已经有一段时间了，并且热爱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a few things that I designed over the years.
zh: 这是我多年来设计的一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's funny because this was really a north star for the Macintosh group.
zh: 这很有趣，因为这真的是 Macintosh 团队的北极星。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I reread it in the last couple of days, it just kind of reminded me of AI and so many things that are being developed now.
zh: 但我在过去几天重读它时，它只是有点让我想起了 AI 和现在正在开发的很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Paul Rand is a celebrated graphic designer, no longer with us, who did the UPS logo and IBM logo and so many images that have persisted.
zh: Paul Rand 是一位著名的平面设计师，已经离我们而去，他设计了 UPS 标志和 IBM 标志以及许多经久不衰的图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was lucky to work with him.
zh: 我很幸运能与他合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And something he told me was always focus on making things meaningful and memorable.
zh: 他告诉我的一件事是，始终专注于让事物有意义且难忘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the heart of that is have a good idea and then the form will follow.
zh: 我认为其核心是要有一个好的想法，然后形式就会随之而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a total art major, didn't know anything about computers, and was lucky enough to work at Apple on the Macintosh as the Macintosh artist.
zh: 我完全是个艺术专业的学生，对电脑一无所知，并且很幸运能在 Apple 作为 Macintosh 艺术家在 Macintosh 上工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And before I went to Apple, I was welding a life-size Razorback hog for a museum in Arkansas.
zh: 在去 Apple 之前，我正在为阿肯色州的一家博物馆焊接一个真人大小的 Razorback 野猪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought I was living my dream, going out to my garage, welding all day.
zh: 我以为我在过梦想中的生活，去我的车库里，整天都在焊接。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in truth, it was a little bit lonely.
zh: 但实际上，这有点孤独。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was glad I had the experience, but it kind of made me hungry for working with a team.
zh: 我很高兴我有这段经历，但这有点让我渴望与团队合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my high school friend, Andy Hertzfeld,
zh: 我的高中朋友，Andy Hertzfeld，

speaker: Unknown
en: was a system software programmer at Apple and he knew I had worked on the yearbook and liked art and he said he needed some images to display on a new computer that was being worked on and he showed me the display which didn't have a case and said could I come in for an interview
zh: 是 Apple 的系统软件程序员，他知道我做过年鉴并喜欢艺术，他说他需要一些图像来显示在一台正在开发的新电脑上，他向我展示了没有外壳的显示器，并问我能否来参加面试

speaker: Unknown
en: To work on some small symbols and some typefaces.
zh: 来制作一些小符号和一些字体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, sure.
zh: 我说，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought it sounded great and really interesting and something I hadn't done before.
zh: 我认为这听起来很棒，真的很有趣，而且是我以前没做过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought about it.
zh: 所以我考虑了一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a little bit...
zh: 我有一点……

speaker: Unknown
en: Of typographical experience from working at the Franklin Institute Science Museum in Philadelphia, I used a machine like this to make labels for exhibits.
zh: 关于在费城富兰克林研究所科学博物馆工作时的排版经验，我使用像这样的机器为展品制作标签。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was pretty good at Letraset, rub-down type.
zh: 我很擅长 Letraset，摩擦转印字。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could do it really straight and get the kerning right.
zh: 我可以把它做得笔直，并且把字距弄对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I went to the, and I had a PhD in art history.
zh: 但我去了，而且我有艺术史的博士学位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those were my credentials.
zh: 所以那些就是我的资历。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I went to the library in Palo Alto and took out some books about typography and some font sample books.
zh: 我去了帕洛阿尔托的图书馆，借了一些关于排版的书和一些字体样本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually brought them to my interview under my arm.
zh: 我实际上把它们夹在腋下带去面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would seem as if I knew what I was talking about.
zh: 这样我看起来就像我知道我在说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: Andy also suggested to me that it would be good if I could make some examples of essentially bitmap graphics but using graph paper and he didn't really specify what to make so some things I made
zh: Andy 也建议我，如果我能制作一些本质上就是位图图形的例子，但是使用方格纸，那就好了，他没有具体说明要做什么，所以我做了一些东西

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a pun with a boot and some pieces of paper.
zh: 像一个关于靴子和几张纸的双关语。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could see on this slide there's a little bit of an ABC.
zh: 你可以在这张幻灯片上看到有一点 ABC 的影子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I just tried to make some examples.
zh: 我只是试着做一些例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are more of the examples.
zh: 而这些是更多的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of funny because some of these really random things slightly influenced what we ended up using in the software.
zh: 有点好笑，因为有些这些真正随机的东西稍微影响了我们最终在软件中使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I spoiled the surprise, but I got the job.
zh: 所以我泄露了惊喜，但我得到了这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think anybody even asked me any questions about font design, despite my prep.
zh: 我认为甚至没有人问我任何关于字体设计的问题，尽管我有准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a funny twist of fate, as much as I had wanted to be an artist, now that notebook with those early icons that I took to my interview is in the permanent collection of MoMA.
zh: 命运有着有趣的转折，尽管我如此想成为一名艺术家，现在那个我带去面试的、带有早期图标的笔记本已经被 MoMA 永久收藏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hang on.
zh: 所以坚持住。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely hang on to your stuff.
zh: 一定要保留你的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I got to Apple the first day, this screen was shown to me to say, this is what it's your job to improve.
zh: 所以当我第一天到达 Apple 时，这个屏幕被展示给我看，上面说，这就是你要改进的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fonts and the round rects that are on the five and a quarter inch floppy drawing are...
zh: 而且字体和五点二五英寸软盘图纸上的圆角矩形是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Could become icons, but they were able with a cursor to click and drag those around.
zh: 可以变成图标，但它们能够用光标点击并拖拽那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it already had a little, seemed kind of magical to me.
zh: 所以它已经有一点，对我来说看起来有点神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we definitely changed do it to okay, because do it was a little off color and people read it as dolt.
zh: 我们肯定把“做它”改成了“好”，因为“做它”有点不雅，人们把它读成“傻瓜”。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wanted to make a new system font and make some icons.
zh: 所以我想制作一个新的系统字体并制作一些图标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, and it was told to me, it was very sincere that we were trying to make a computer that anyone could use, so I felt good about that because I was in that group.
zh: 所以，有人告诉过我，非常真诚地，我们正试图制造一台任何人都能使用的电脑，所以我对此感觉很好，因为我在那个组里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even though I am happy to work on and have worked on many projects that weren't for me, but I like that about this project.
zh: 虽然我很乐意参与，并且也参与了很多不是为我而做的项目，但我喜欢这个项目的这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we wanted it to be as understandable as possible so you wouldn't necessarily need a manual.
zh: 我们希望它尽可能易懂，这样你不一定需要手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that it should be friendly because there were so many people there in the Mac software group where I was who were just passionate about computers and kind of wanted to be evangelical about that.
zh: 而且它应该是友好的，因为我在的 Mac 软件组里有很多人只是对电脑充满热情，并且有点想要对此进行传道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there were a few constraints, and usually I think you can be creative in any constraints.
zh: 所以有一些限制，通常我认为你可以在任何限制下发挥创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make some pretty fun art with beach trash while you're walking around.
zh: 当你四处走动时，你可以用海滩垃圾制作一些相当有趣的艺术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this...
zh: 还有这...

speaker: Unknown
en: You can be creative, but it's good to understand what the constraints are and then be excited about that as opposed to being upset that you don't have a thousand colors.
zh: 你可以发挥创造力，但最好明白限制是什么，然后对此感到兴奋，而不是因为你没有一千种颜色而感到沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is 16 by 16 black and white.
zh: 所以这是 16 乘 16 的黑白。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the first images that I made using those constraints were things like this.
zh: 我认为我在使用那些限制时制作的第一批图像就是像这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought about, you know, thought maybe a lasso would be a good way to surround an irregular region and some other art tools.
zh: 我们考虑过，你知道，想也许套索会是包围不规则区域的好方法，还有一些其他的艺术工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's funny to me because I went to Paris for the first time fairly recently and there's a street artist known as Space Invader and he does a lot of mosaic work and he has borrowed liberally from early Macintosh stuff which made me really happy.
zh: 这对我来说很有趣，因为我在最近第一次去了巴黎，那里有一位被称为 Space Invader 的街头艺术家，他做了很多马赛克作品，他大量借鉴了早期的 Macintosh 的东西，这让我真的很高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first font I designed was Chicago.
zh: 所以我设计的第一个字体是 Chicago。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's nine pixels tall, cap height, and
zh: 它有九个像素高，大写字母高度，而且

speaker: Unknown
en: I looked at the stuff that was on the screen and it just seemed as if it was all jaggedy and it didn't seem as if it would be that big a deal to make it look tidier by using horizontals and verticals and 45 degree angles.
zh: 我看着屏幕上的东西，它看起来似乎全是锯齿状的，似乎通过使用水平线、垂直线和 45 度角让它看起来更整洁并不是什么大不了的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I still wince when I look at especially at that lowercase x.
zh: 所以当我看那个小写 x 时我仍然会退缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the others I could pretty much fit into the system.
zh: 但其他的我几乎都可以放入系统中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were so lucky on the Macintosh to be able to do proportionally spaced fonts.
zh: 我们在 Macintosh 上非常幸运能够做到比例间距字体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I could remember just seeing displays where the M was really squished and then the I was really wide.
zh: 因为我可以记得看到的显示中，M 被挤压得很扁，而 I 又很宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I didn't realize what a big deal this advancement was, but it seemed to make it look a lot better.
zh: 所以我并没有意识到这一进步有多大，但它似乎确实让它看起来好多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we used Chicago, we put it in the title bar, experimented a lot till we came up with those lines.
zh: 所以我们使用了 Chicago，把它放在标题栏里，做了很多实验，直到我们想出了那些线条。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we didn't realize was that when we designed the calculator that we were designing the first iPod, which also used Chicago, which made me happy.
zh: 我们没有意识到的是，当我们设计计算器时，我们实际上是在设计第一台 iPod，它也使用了 Chicago，这让我很高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we shipped some other fonts with the Mac, including a monospace font.
zh: 我们随 Mac 一起发布了一些其他字体，包括一个等宽字体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was able to kind of think, well, we should probably have a Times Roman kind of thing and a Helvetica kind of thing.
zh: 但我能够想，好吧，我们可能应该有一个 Times Roman 类型的东西和一个 Helvetica 类型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's where New York and Geneva came from.
zh: 这就是 New York 和 Geneva 的由来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I made a font that...
zh: 然后我做了一个字体...

speaker: Unknown
en: I called Ransom because it was what kidnappers used to do by cutting letters out of the newspaper so they wouldn't have to reveal their handwriting and get caught.
zh: 我称之为 Ransom，因为这是绑架者过去常做的事，从报纸上剪下字母，这样他们就不必暴露自己的笔迹而被抓。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like the other fonts, Andy and I gave them city names.
zh: 就像其他字体一样，Andy 和我给它们起了城市的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because we had gone to high school near Philadelphia, we gave them names of
zh: 因为我们曾在费城附近上高中，所以我们给它们取了

speaker: Unknown
en: Towns on the Paoli local through the suburbs into the city.
zh: Paoli 本地列车经过郊区进入城市的沿途城镇的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Steve Jobs came by one afternoon.
zh: 一天下午 Steve Jobs 过来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He usually came by at the end of the day and walked around software group to see what was new.
zh: 他通常在一天结束时过来，在软件组四处走走，看看有什么新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, well, city names aren't bad, but at least call them world-class cities.
zh: 他说，好吧，城市名字也不坏，但至少要叫世界级的城市。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's how we ended up with New York and Geneva instead of...
zh: 这就是我们最后用了 New York 和 Geneva 而不是...

speaker: Unknown
en: Paoli and Wynwood and Rosemont, where our high school was.
zh: Paoli、Wynwood 和 Rosemont，我们高中所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Bill Atkinson was the programmer who wrote MacPaint, and that was my favorite program, of course, and was happy to collaborate on the icons and the patterns.
zh: Bill Atkinson 是编写 MacPaint 的程序员，那当然是我最喜欢的程序，并且很高兴能合作设计图标和图案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he developed an early scanner, and that's how we got this geisha image from a woodcut that Steve Jobs owned.
zh: 他开发了一种早期的扫描仪，这就是我们从 Steve Jobs 拥有的一幅木版画中得到这张艺妓图像的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we made a control panel that had animation for when you changed the settings, hoping to communicate what would happen and what your choices were.
zh: 我们制作了一个控制面板，当你更改设置时会有动画，希望能传达将会发生什么以及你的选择是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we tried, obviously, not to use, we could use sound, we could use speed, but we tried not to have any text so that it could be international without having to make a different version.
zh: 显然我们试图，不使用，我们可以使用声音，我们可以使用速度，但我们试图没有任何文字，这样它就可以是国际化的而不必制作不同的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, we didn't have that many really great tools for art, but whatever.
zh: 而且，你知道，我们没有那么多真正好的艺术工具，但是管他呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We forged ahead.
zh: 我们继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Andy wrote, I did not have to design on graph paper once I got to Apple.
zh: Andy 写道，一旦我到了 Apple，我就不需要在方格纸上设计了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Andy wrote an icon editor.
zh: Andy 写了一个图标编辑器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is an image writer, a picture of an image writer print of what the screen looked like with the icon editor.
zh: 这是一台 ImageWriter，是一张 ImageWriter 打印出来的屏幕上图标编辑器样子的图片。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were no tools.
zh: 没有任何工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could just toggle the bits and you could see a greatly enlarged image as well as what the icon looked like at 72 DPI.
zh: 你可以只是切换位，你可以看到一个放大的图像，以及图标在 72 DPI 下的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought this was just magical, even though it didn't have 20 levels of undo and you couldn't draw any shapes.
zh: 我认为这简直太神奇了，即使它没有 20 级撤销，你也无法绘制任何形状。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could iterate without an eraser.
zh: 你可以在没有橡皮擦的情况下进行迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to overstate how great this was.
zh: 这有多好简直难以言表。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it automatically generated the hex code for an icon, which I could then type in and see the image on the screen.
zh: 它自动为图标生成十六进制代码，然后我可以输入并在屏幕上看到图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a marvel.
zh: 所以这是一个奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: This icon isn't crying.
zh: 这个图标没有在哭。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was probably me counting pixels for some reason down the edge.
zh: 可能是我为了某种原因在边缘数像素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see in the title bar, we tried a bunch of different types of things during the time we were experimenting.
zh: 在标题栏中你可以看到，在我们实验期间尝试了一堆不同类型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes I liked to, people came and sat and I would do their portrait in 32 by 32.
zh: 有时我喜欢这样，人们过来坐下，我会用 32x32 的尺寸给他们画肖像。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people seemed to enjoy that.
zh: 所以人们似乎很享受那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there wasn't really a way to get a photo in there at the time or even a drawing.
zh: 当时并没有真正的方法把照片放进去，甚至是一幅画。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just had to do it from life.
zh: 所以只能写生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I still enjoy making those portraits.
zh: 我仍然享受制作那些肖像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's kind of amazing that in a thousand dots, if you iterate a lot, you can get an image with some semblance of resemblance.
zh: 我觉得这很神奇，在一千个点里，如果你迭代很多次，你可以得到一个有一定相似外观的图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see Pharrell Williams is at the top on the right and Ashton Kutcher under him.
zh: 你可以看到 Pharrell Williams 在顶部右边，Ashton Kutcher 在他下面。

speaker: Unknown
en: They did not sit for their portrait.
zh: 他们没有坐下来画肖像。

speaker: Unknown
en: some people that aren't super well known and John Maeda who's a design leader the one thing that
zh: 一些不是很出名的人，还有 John Maeda，他是设计领导者，唯一的一件事是

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the first icons I was assigned was it took a while for the computer to boot when it got turned on so everybody wanted an image on the screen and it had to be 32 by 32 because it was only 128k Macintosh.
zh: 我被分配到的第一批图标之一是，当电脑开机时启动需要一段时间，所以每个人都想要屏幕上有一个图像，它必须是 32x32，因为它只有 128k 的 Macintosh。

speaker: Unknown
en: So because the computer was sitting there kind of grinding while it started up, we wanted something that showed that everything was okay.
zh: 所以因为电脑坐在那里在启动时有点嘎吱作响，我们想要某种显示一切正常的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought a smile was good.
zh: 所以我认为微笑很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm pretty sure it came from my memory of a button I got when I was about 14.
zh: 我很确定它来自我大约 14 岁时得到的一个按钮的记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like smiling and happy things.
zh: 我喜欢微笑和快乐的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Understanding Happy Mac is a play on the title of this excellent book by Scott McCloud, which is about comics, but really has so many good insights about user interface too.
zh: 理解 Happy Mac 是对 Scott McCloud 这本优秀书名的戏仿，它是关于漫画的，但实际上也有很多关于用户界面的好见解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It came out 10 years after the Mac originally did.
zh: 它在 Mac 最初推出 10 年后才出版。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I pulled two illustrations from that book by Scott McCloud that kind of explains some of the thinking behind our icons, which is that when a face in particular has a lot of detail,
zh: 我从 Scott McCloud 的那本书里拿了两张插图，解释了一些我们图标背后的想法，那就是当一张脸有很多细节时，

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks like somebody else.
zh: 它看起来像别人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you make it really simple, everyone can project themselves onto it.
zh: 但如果你把它做得非常简单，每个人都可以把自己投射到它上面。
